purpose: Can a fraction change its name without changing its length?
meaning: A rational number is expressible as a quotient of two integers with a nonzero denominator. Divide numerator and positive denominator by their greatest common divisor. The reduced fraction has the same value, including zero and negative balances.

definition.setting: A ribbon account records a pieces, each 1/b metre long. Positive pieces are held; negative pieces are owed. The reduced fraction names the same signed length.

signature.b: Positive number of equal pieces making one metre.
signature.p: Numerator after canceling the common divisor.
signature.q: Positive denominator after canceling the common divisor.
signature.d: Common positive divisor used to reduce both parts.

conditions: The numerator is an integer from −12 to 12 and the denominator is a positive integer from 1 to 12. Exact fraction strings remain distinct from their rounded decimal displays.

properties.claim: Canceling a common nonzero factor preserves a fraction.
properties.conditions: The numerator is an integer from −12 to 12 and the denominator is a positive integer from 1 to 12. Exact fraction strings remain distinct from their rounded decimal displays.
properties.derivation: If a=dp and b=dq with d positive, then a/b=(dp)/(dq)=p/q. The denominator remains nonzero.

examples.title: Rename six eighths
examples.question: Can a fraction change its name without changing its length?
examples.setting: A ribbon account holds or owes a whole number of equal pieces. The denominator says how many pieces make one metre. Move either input and compare the original fraction with its reduced name at the same signed number-line position.
assumptions: The numerator is an integer from −12 to 12 and the denominator is a positive integer from 1 to 12. Exact fraction strings remain distinct from their rounded decimal displays.

steps.reason: Divide numerator and positive denominator by their greatest common divisor. The reduced fraction has the same value, including zero and negative balances.

examples.interpretation: Cancel two from numerator and denominator; the length stays three quarters of a metre.

independent_check.method: Cross-multiply the original and reduced fractions: 6 × 4 = 8 × (3) = 24. The reduced numerator and denominator share no positive divisor above 1.
